# SK2102 — The `[DebuggerDisplay]` string names a member that does not exist

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `{…}` hole in a `[DebuggerDisplay]` string on a type declaration names a single identifier that is not a member of that type or of anything it inherits or implements.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S4545 |

## Why

The expression is bound by the debugger at inspection time, not by the compiler, so a rename breaks it silently and it is discovered while debugging something else, at the moment it is least welcome. It is the same string-to-member binding `nameof` exists to remove, and the same class of defect as an `ArgumentException` naming a parameter that is not there. There is no fix: only the author knows which member was meant, and a rule that guessed would rename the display to whatever happened to be nearby.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
[DebuggerDisplay("{Title,nq}")]
sealed class Book {
    public string Name { get; init; } = "";
}
```

Write:

```csharp
[DebuggerDisplay("{Name,nq}")]
sealed class Book {
    public string Name { get; init; } = "";
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The text inside the braces is a limited expression language, not a member name**, and a parser that guesses at it produces false positives on correct code. The accepted grammar is therefore deliberately tiny: one identifier, with an optional `this.` in front and an optional `,nq`-style all-letters format specifier behind. ⚠ **Anything else withdraws the whole attribute rather than the one hole** — a call, an index, an operator, a literal, a further `.`, a nested brace, an unbalanced brace, a comma this parser cannot account for. A string this parser only half understands is a string it has no standing to report on. ⚠ **The dotted path is the exclusion that matters most**: `{Owner.Name}` would need the member's type to answer and `{DateTime.Now}` has a root that is not a member of anything, so reporting either would be wrong for a different reason each time. ⚠ **An explicit interface implementation is stored under a mangled name** (`ICollection.Count`), so the lookup matches a member whose name ends in `.` plus the identifier as well as one that equals it; without that, a type whose only `Count` is explicitly implemented would be reported for correct code. Interfaces implemented and base types are searched, and **an error type anywhere on that chain withdraws the answer entirely** — an unresolved base reads as "no such member" and reporting it would be silently wrong, which is also why the rule finds nothing on a source slice with no dependency closure (#277). Only a class, struct, record or record struct declaration is examined; `[DebuggerDisplay]` also targets a field, a property and an assembly, and on those the expression binds against something other than the annotated declaration. The argument must be a compile-time constant string. Generated code is excluded.

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2102.severity`
